questions.question: Which color should you wear to be more visible?
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green when riding. These colors make you easier to see at any time of day.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol, you should:

options.text: Decide if you can ride based on how you feel after drinking.
Set a drinking limit so you can still ride safely.
Not worry about riding if you feel fine.

questions.explanation: Do not ride after drinking alcohol. Even small amounts of alcohol can affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Always look ahead and watch for dangers.
Look at your controls and speedometer instead of the road.
Not worry about dangers on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always look ahead and watch for dangers.
questions.explanation: Look well ahead while riding to spot dangers early. This gives you time to react before problems happen.

questions.question: For the best protection, your helmet must:
questions.explanation: Your helmet must meet U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly around your head with no defects.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders should wear shoes with soles that:
questions.explanation: Wear riding boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles. The soles should be hard, durable, and slip-resistant.

questions.question: To help other drivers see you, wear:
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors to be seen by other drivers. Bright clothes help you stay visible day and night.

questions.question: When you see a bump or pothole, rise slightly off your seat:

options.text: So you can jump off if needed.
So your legs can absorb the impact.
So other drivers can see you better.
So you can see the uneven surface better.

questions.correctAnswerText: So your legs can absorb the impact.
questions.explanation: Rising off your seat lets your legs absorb some of the shock. This prevents the impact from throwing you off the motorcycle.

questions.question: A plastic face shield protects you from:
questions.explanation: A face shield protects your face from wind, dust, dirt, rain, insects, and rocks thrown from other vehicles.

questions.question: Before riding, check your tires for all of the following except:
questions.explanation: Check your tire air pressure, tread depth, and general wear before each ride.

questions.question: To lower your crash risk, you should:

options.text: Tell other drivers what you plan to do.
Ride where drivers cannot see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Reduce crash risk by staying visible and signaling your actions. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to communicate. Keep space around your motorcycle and constantly watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, what should motorcycle riders watch out for?

options.text: Drivers looking for a parking spot.
Cars pulling out of parking spaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cars pulling out of parking spaces.
questions.explanation: When passing parked vehicles, be careful. Cars may pull away from the curb or leave parking spaces without warning.

questions.question: If hazards are on your left, where should you ride?

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
In any portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the right portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When hazards are on your left, ride in the right portion of the lane. Change your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: What should you do when riding a motorcycle on a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, reduce your speed. Use both brakes when braking and avoid sudden movements.

questions.question: If another driver is following too close, what should you do?

options.text: Move to one side of your lane to let them share it.

questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them ahead of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may increase danger by encouraging them to tailgate you at higher speeds.

questions.question: Where should you get information about your motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Your owner's manual is your best source for information about your specific motorcycle. It includes details about how it works, how to operate it, and what maintenance it needs.

questions.question: If you wait one hour for each drink before riding, will alcohol effects be gone?

options.text: Yes, your skills will not be affected.

questions.explanation: Your body can eliminate about one drink per hour. However, alcohol can still build up in your system even at this rate. This buildup can affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: What is usually found in the center of a lane?
questions.explanation: Car drippings create an oily strip in the center of each lane. On dry roads, it is usually safe for a motorcycle to ride on this strip.

questions.question: How should a helmet fit for the best protection?
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly all around with no visible damage.

questions.question: If a friend has had too much to drink and wants to ride, what should you do?

options.text: Tell them to use quiet roads.

questions.explanation: Never let someone ride after drinking too much. Stop them however you can, including taking their keys. Help them find another way to get home.

questions.question: Which organization certifies helmets for maximum protection?
questions.explanation: Use a motorcycle helmet certified by the U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) for maximum protection.

questions.question: During the day, you should:

options.text: Use your headlight only when it is cloudy.
Use your headlight if you want to.

questions.explanation: Always use your headlight when riding, even during the day. This makes other drivers twice as likely to see you.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: A face shield:

options.text: Does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, impact-resistant face shield provides the best protection for your eyes and face. Regular eyeglasses or sunglasses are not enough protection. In Vermont, you are not required by law to wear eye or face protection if your motorcycle has a windshield, but it is still recommended.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Not wear a jacket if it is warm.
Always wear a jacket, even in warm weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always wear a jacket, even in warm weather.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket when riding, even in warm weather. It protects you and helps prevent dehydration. Also wear long pants and tuck in your shoelaces so they do not catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: The best lane position is:

options.text: One that lets you go the fastest.
One that lets you draft off other vehicles.
One that makes other drivers see you.
One that places you in blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: One that makes other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that helps other drivers see you and helps you see them. This also helps you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. Good lane position discourages sharing your lane and gives you an escape route. Position yourself to have the most space around you.
